top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) ranks first on the common criteria. His voice is recognizable within a page, with long, rhythmically driven, hallucinatory sentences. As far as public knowledge shows, the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid are built as large architectures that join memory, the body, Bucharest and metaphysical speculation across decades. The citation should rest on the prose and name poetry only as its root, since the poetry and early work are unevenly covered in translation. The main unresolved risk is whether the late novels vary or recycle imagery. I cannot settle that from translation and have not verified the Romanian originals. Carson (P002) is a serious second choice: her line-level control and formal invention are real, and a citation limited to original poetry, essay and hybrid narrative answers most of the translation-scope worry. I still cannot tell which works beyond Autobiography of Red and Nox form a durable core, or how much of Nox's effect depends on book design. Both cases would benefit from expert readers of the originals and of the later volumes. No award (P000) ranks last because both proposals rest on substantial literary achievement.
